commands.name: GetAddOnVersion
commands.description: Retrieves the version of the Tapir Additional JSON Commands Add-On.

commands.name: GetArchicadLocation
commands.description: Retrieves the location of the currently running Archicad executable.

commands.name: QuitArchicad
commands.description: Performs a quit operation on the currently running Archicad instance.

commands.name: GetPointFromUser
commands.description: Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled.

prompt.description: Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.

commands.name: GetCurrentWindowType
commands.description: Returns the type of the current (active) window.

commands.name: ChangeWindow
commands.description: Changes the current (active) window to the given window. With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan.

commands.name: GetUserGSID
commands.description: Get the current registered User-GSID and OrganizationsID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: ShowAlert
commands.description: Display a dialog with up to three buttons.

alertType.description: The type of the alert dialog.

title.description: The title of the alert dialog.

subMessage.description: Optional smaller sub-message text below the main message.

button2.description: Label for the second button (e.g. Cancel).

button3.description: Label for the optional third button.

commands.name: GetSpecialFolders
commands.description: Retrieves the filesystem paths of the special folders of the running Archicad (preferences, cache, data, temporary, application, defaults, templates, help, embedded project library, etc.).

folderTypes.description: The types of the special folders to retrieve.

commands.name: GetProjectInfo
commands.description: Retrieves information about the currently loaded project.

commands.name: GetProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Retrieves the names and values of all project info fields.

commands.name: SetProjectInfoField
commands.description: Sets the value of a project info field.

projectInfoId.description: The id of the project info field.

projectInfoValue.description: The new value of the project info field. An empty string clears the field.

commands.name: CreateProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Creates one or more custom project info fields.

projectInfoFields.description: Array of custom project info fields to create.

commands.name: DeleteProjectInfoFields
commands.description: Deletes one or more custom project info fields. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted.

projectInfoIds.description: List of project info field ids to delete. Only custom fields (ids starting with 'autotext-') can be deleted.

commands.name: GetStories
commands.description: Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.

commands.name: SetStories
commands.description: Sets the story sructure of the currently loaded project.

commands.name: GetAutoTextKeys
commands.description: Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key), optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'.

elementId.description: Optional. The element to retrieve context dependent autotext keys for (its own properties, plus the ones common to all element types, e.g. 'Element ID', 'Area'). When omitted, only the autotext keys common to all element types are returned.

commands.name: GetAutoTextName
commands.description: Retrieves the display names of one or more autotext keys (as returned inside a '<...>' embedded key), with a direct guid lookup for property-based keys instead of enumerating every property definition.

keys.description: Autotext keys as returned by GetAutoTextKeys or GetProjectInfoFields (without the surrounding '<' and '>'), e.g. 'PROPERTY-69A58F6F-DD3B-478D-B5EF-09A16BD0C548' or 'PROJECTNAME'.

commands.name: GetHotlinks
commands.description: Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.

commands.name: CreateHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink module nodes to create. A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).

name.description: Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

storyRangeType.description: Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

refFloorIndex.description: Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

commands.name: CreateHotlinkInstances
commands.description: Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring.

commands.name: ChangeHotlinkInstances
commands.description: Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances.

hotlinkInstances.description: The placed hotlink instances to change. Every field but elementId is optional; a field that is omitted keeps its current value.

commands.name: UpdateHotlinks
commands.description: Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to update, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. Each node's cached content is re-read from its source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

commands.name: ChangeHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content.

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to repoint at another source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. The placed instances stay where they are. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks on the same nodes to re-read the content from the new file.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the new module source file (.mod or .pln).

commands.name: OpenProject
commands.description: Opens the given project.

projectFilePath.description: The target project file to open.

commands.name: CloseProject
commands.description: Closes the currently opened project.

commands.name: SaveProject
commands.description: Saves the currently opened project.

projectPath.description: Optional. Full path of a .pln file to save the project to, as File > Save As does: the open project then refers to that file. This saves an untitled project, or one opened from an older Archicad version, which cannot be saved in place. An existing file at the path is overwritten. When omitted, or when it is the project's own file, the project is saved in place, which keeps the refusal of a project opened read-only.

commands.name: SaveAsModuleFile
commands.description: Saves the given elements, or the current selection, as a hotlink module (.mod) file.

moduleFilePath.description: Absolute path of the .mod file to write. An existing file is overwritten. The current window must be a floor plan, section, elevation or detail.

elements.description: Optional. The elements that go into the module; omitted, the current selection does, as Save Selection as Module would. Pass GetAllElements for the whole project. Archicad 25 and 26 support the selection form only.

commands.name: SaveProjectAsArchive
commands.description: Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside.

archiveFilePath.description: Absolute path of the .pla archive to write. An existing file is overwritten. The archive becomes the open project, as Save As does.

includeLibraryParts.description: Optional, true by default. Whether the library parts the project uses go into the archive, which makes the archive usable as a linked library of another project.

includeProperties.description: Optional, true by default. Whether the properties go into the archive.

includeTextures.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the linked textures go into the archive.

includeBackgroundPicture.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the background picture goes into the archive.

commands.name: SaveCurrentWindowAsImage
commands.description: Saves what the current window shows as an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif), as File > Save as does with a picture format.

imageFilePath.description: Absolute path of the image file to write. An existing file is overwritten.

format.description: Optional. The image file format; omitted, it comes from the extension of imageFilePath (.png, .jpg or .jpeg, .bmp, .tif or .tiff, .gif).

colorDepth.description: Optional, trueColor by default. The color depth of the image, as in the Save as picture dialog.

dithered.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the image is dithered when its color depth drops colors.

entireDrawing.description: Optional, false by default. Whether the image covers the entire drawing of a 2D window instead of its current zoom, as the Entire Drawing option of the Save as picture dialog does.

commands.name: GetCalculationUnits
commands.description: Gets the project calculation units.

commands.name: GetGeoLocation
commands.description: Gets the project location details.

commands.name: SetGeoLocation
commands.description: Sets the project location details.

commands.name: PrintView
commands.description: Prints from the current view.

grid.description: Print the grid. The default is false.

fixText.description: Use fixed text size. The default is false.

printArea.description: The area to print. The default is 'currentView'.

commands.name: RebuildView
commands.description: Rebuilds the current view.

regenerate.description: Regenerate the view. The default is false, meaning the view will not be regenerated, but rebuilt.

commands.name: GetSelectedElements
commands.description: Gets the list of the currently selected elements.

commands.name: GetElementsByType
commands.description: Returns the identifier of every element of the given type on the plan. It works for any type. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering.

commands.name: GetAllElements
commands.description: Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering.

commands.name: ChangeSelectionOfElements
commands.description: Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection.

commands.name: FilterElements
commands.description: Tests an elements by the given criterias.

commands.name: GetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the details of the given elements (geometry parameters etc). Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons).

fields.description: Optional filter for the fields to return for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.

commands.name: SetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Sets the details of the given elements (floor, layer, order etc).

commands.name: Get3DBoundingBoxes
commands.description: Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements.

commands.name: Get3DGeometryOfElements
commands.description: Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.

commands.name: GetQuantitiesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values.

minOpeningSize.description: Optional minimum opening size in square meters. Openings smaller than this are not subtracted when the conditional values (for example volumeConditional of a Wall) are calculated. Archicad only uses it for walls. Default value is 0, so every opening is subtracted.

commands.name: GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements
commands.description: Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements.

commands.name: GetConnectedElements
commands.description: Gets the elements hosted by (connected to) the given owner elements, filtered to the given element type: for example the Windows or Doors of a Wall, the frames, panels, junctions and accessories of a Curtain Wall, the risers, treads and structures of a Stair, or the posts, rails and panels of a Railing.

elements.description: The owner (host) elements whose connected elements are collected, e.g. Walls, Curtain Walls, Stairs or Railings.

connectedElementType.description: The type of the connected elements to collect, e.g. Window or Door for a Wall owner, or a subelement type of a Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing owner.

commands.name: GetSectionElements
commands.description: Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires.

databases.description: The section, elevation or interior elevation databases to list the section elements of. If omitted, the current database is used.

commands.name: GetRelationsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the type-specific relations of the given elements: endpoint and reference line connections of walls, beams and beam segments, boundary elements and boundary sections of zones, the zones on the two sides of windows, doors, skylights and curtain wall panels, and the zones connected to roofs and shells. Available from Archicad 26.

otherElementType.description: Optional filter: only relations to elements of this type are returned.

commands.name: GetZoneBoundaries
commands.description: Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone.

zoneElementId.description: The identifier of a single Zone. Prefer the zones array: querying many Zones in one call is much faster than one call per Zone.

zones.description: A list of Zones. Only one of zoneElementId and zones can be given.

commands.name: UpdateZones
commands.description: Updates all Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements).

keepStampPosition.description: Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default is true.

undoTopTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default is false.

undoBottomTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The default is false.

commands.name: GetCollisions
commands.description: Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements.

volumeTolerance.description: Intersection body volume greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

performSurfaceCheck.description: Enables surface collision check. If disabled the surfaceTolerance value will be ignored. By default it's false.

surfaceTolerance.description: Intersection body surface area greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

commands.name: HighlightElements
commands.description: Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights.

highlightedColors.description: A list of colors to highlight elements.

items.description: Color of the highlighted element as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

wireframe3D.description: Optional parameter. Switch non highlighted elements in the 3D window to wireframe.

nonHighlightedColor.description: Optional parameter. Color of the non highlighted elements as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

commands.name: MoveElements
commands.description: Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

elementsWithMoveVectors.description: The elements with move vector pairs.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be moved. By default it's false.

commands.name: RotateElements
commands.description: Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

beginPoint.description: Starting point of the rotation arc.

endPoint.description: End point of the rotation arc.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a copy of the element is rotated. By default it's false.

commands.name: DeleteElements
commands.description: Deletes elements. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently.

commands.name: LockElements
commands.description: Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

commands.name: UnlockElements
commands.description: Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

commands.name: GetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements.

commands.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements.

elementsWithGDLParameters.description: The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.

commands.name: GetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns.

commands.name: SetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are.

elementsWithMarkerParameters.description: The elements with the marker parameters to change.

markerParameters.description: The marker parameters to change, each given by name or by index. The other marker parameters and the opening's own settings are left as they are.

name.description: The name of the marker parameter.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter: a number for the numeric types (Integer, Length, Angle, RealNumber, PenColor, LineType, Material, FillPattern, BuildingMaterial, Profile, RGBColor, Intensity), a string for String and Title, true/false for Boolean and 'On'/'Off' for LightSwitch. Array parameters are not supported.

index.description: The index of the marker parameter, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements reports it.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter, see the value given with a name.

commands.name: CreateColumns
commands.description: Creates Column elements based on the given parameters.

columnsData.description: Array of data to create Columns.

items.description: The parameters of the new Column.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

height.description: Optional column height.

axisRotationAngle.description: Optional column rotation angle in radians.

slantAngle.description: Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

slantDirectionAngle.description: Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

commands.name: CreateWalls
commands.description: Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.

floorIndex.description: Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.

height.description: Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.

thickness.description: Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

offset.description: Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

referenceLineLocation.description: Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.

structureType.description: Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

linkToSettings.description: When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

commands.name: CreateBeams
commands.description: Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

slantAngle.description: Slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also switches the beam to slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

profileAngle.description: Rotation angle of the profile around the beam's center line, in radians.

arcAngle.description: Optional arc angle in radians. A non-zero value makes a horizontally curved beam.

verticalCurveHeight.description: Optional rise of a vertically curved beam. A non-zero value makes a vertically curved beam; it wins over arcAngle.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

commands.name: CreateStairs
commands.description: Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters.

stairsData.description: Array of data to create Stair elements.

items.description: The parameters of the new Stair.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

finishVisible.description: Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

commands.name: CreateSlabs
commands.description: Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters.

slabsData.description: Array of data to create Slabs.

items.description: The parameters of the new Slab.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

level.description: The Z coordinate value of the reference line of the slab.

thickness.description: Optional slab thickness. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType, buildingMaterialId or compositeId the new slab keeps the structure of the slab tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

structureType.description: Optional structure of the slab. If omitted, derived from buildingMaterialId or compositeId when one is given, otherwise the slab tool default (or the favorite) is kept.

buildingMaterialId.description: Building material of a Basic slab. Cannot be combined with compositeId.

compositeId.description: Composite attribute of a Composite slab. Cannot be combined with buildingMaterialId.

referencePlaneLocation.description: For a basic (homogeneous) slab only 'Top' or 'Bottom' are valid.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the edge of the slab.

polygonArcs.description: Polygon outline arcs of the slab.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

commands.name: CreateWindows
commands.description: Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

libraryPartName.description: Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a window library part. Applied to the tool defaults before cloning.

favoriteName.description: Optional. Name of an existing Window favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Window tool defaults before the create.

commands.name: CreateDoors
commands.description: Creates Door elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

libraryPartName.description: Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a door library part. Applied to the tool defaults before cloning.

favoriteName.description: Optional. Name of an existing Door favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Door tool defaults before the create.

commands.name: CreateOpenings
commands.description: Creates Opening elements in the given host elements.

commands.name: CreateMorphs
commands.description: Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions.

size.description: Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.

body.description: Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.

topExpansion.description: Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

commands.name: CreateRoofs
commands.description: Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

pivotLine.description: If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.

angle.description: Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.

commands.name: CreateCurtainWalls
commands.description: Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

curtainWallsData.description: Array of data to create Curtain Walls.

items.description: The parameters of the new Curtain Wall. Everything not given here - the frame and panel classes, the surfaces, the boundary and corner frames, the pattern - comes from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults of the open project.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.

zCoordinate.description: Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.

levelDimensionsData.description: Array of data to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan).

profileType.description: slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is set to Slanted.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

commands.name: GetIFCTypeOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC types of the given elements.

commands.name: GetIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC properties of the given elements.

commands.name: SetIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCPropertyValues.description: The IFC property values to set. Only single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties are supported.

propertySetName.description: The name of the property set, for example Pset_DoorCommon. Custom property set names are also accepted.

propertyName.description: The name of the property, for example FireRating.

type.description: The IFC type of the value, for example IfcLabel, IfcText, IfcIdentifier, IfcBoolean, IfcLogical, IfcInteger, IfcReal or a measure type like IfcThermalTransmittanceMeasure.

value.description: The new value of the property. Provide a boolean for IfcBoolean and IfcLogical (IfcLogical also accepts the string Unknown), a number for the numeric types and a string for every other type.

commands.name: GetLibraries
commands.description: Gets the list of loaded libraries.

commands.name: ReloadLibraries
commands.description: Executes the reload libraries command.

commands.name: AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary
commands.description: Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

overwriteExisting.description: Optional. When true, an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is deleted first, so the newly added file replaces the loaded library part. By default false: the existing loaded part stays in use. Requires Archicad 27 or newer.

commands.name: DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems
commands.description: Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27.

embeddedLibraryItems.description: A list of embedded library items to delete.

path.description: The relative path of the library item inside the embedded library, the same path AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath.

commands.name: SetLibraries
commands.description: Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear.

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

commands.name: AddLibraries
commands.description: Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded.

libraries.description: Local library folders or container files, by absolute path.

commands.name: GetAvailableLibraryParts
commands.description: Lists library parts currently available to the project. Filter by typeId (e.g. 'Door', 'Window', 'Object', 'Lamp').

filterByTypeId.description: Optional. Filter by libpart type (matches the value returned by LibPartTypeIdToString).

commands.name: TeamworkSend
commands.description: Performs a send operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.

commands.name: TeamworkReceive
commands.description: Performs a receive operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.

commands.name: ReserveElements
commands.description: Reserves elements in Teamwork mode.

commands.name: ReleaseElements
commands.description: Releases elements in Teamwork mode.

commands.name: ReserveLockableObjectSet
commands.description: Reserves a non-element lockable object set (attributes, favorites, project info, project preferences, etc.) in Teamwork mode. The object set is given by its Archicad API name, e.g. 'Composites', 'LayerSettingsDialog' or 'ProjectInfo'.

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

commands.name: ReleaseLockableObjectSet
commands.description: Releases a non-element lockable object set reserved with ReserveLockableObjectSet in Teamwork mode.

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

commands.name: GetLockableObjectSetStatus
commands.description: Returns the Teamwork reservation status of a non-element lockable object set and the users who hold it.

objectSetName.description: The name of the lockable object set, as the Archicad API documents it: BuildingMaterials, Cities, Composites, Favorites, FillTypes, LayerSettingsDialog (layers and layer combinations), LineTypes, MarkupStyles, MEPSystems, ModelViewOptions, OperationProfiles, PenTables, Profiles, ProjectInfo, GeoLocation (project location), PreferencesDialog (project preferences and dimension standards), GraphicOverrides (renovation override styles), Surfaces or ZoneCategories. Other names the Archicad API accepts work too.

commands.name: ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement
commands.description: Reserves the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode, which is needed before changing hotlink nodes.

commands.name: ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement
commands.description: Releases the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode.

commands.name: PublishPublisherSet
commands.description: Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set.

outputPath.description: Full local or LAN path for publishing. Optional, by default the path set in the settings of the publisher set will be used.

selectedNavigatorItemIds.description: Optional publisher-tree navigator items to publish instead of the whole publisher set.

commands.name: UpdateDrawings
commands.description: Performs a drawing update on the given elements.

commands.name: GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId
commands.description: Gets the ID of the database associated with the supplied navigator item id

commands.name: CreateDetails
commands.description: Creates independent Detail databases.

commands.name: CreateWorksheets
commands.description: Creates independent Worksheet databases.

commands.name: CreateLayout
commands.description: Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts.

paperWidth.description: Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.

paperHeight.description: Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.

commands.name: CreateLayoutSubset
commands.description: Creates Layout Book subsets.

commands.name: CreateDrawings
commands.description: Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

name.description: Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.

nameType.description: Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.

scale.description: Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

drawingScale.description: The nominal scale of the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

modelOffset.description: Offset of the model origin within the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.

commands.name: ChangeDrawingLink
commands.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation).

items.description: An existing Drawing and the navigator item it should be relinked to.

commands.name: GetLayoutSettings
commands.description: Gets settings of layouts, including Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

commands.name: SetLayoutSettings
commands.description: Sets settings of layouts, including Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

commands.name: GetLayoutCustomScheme
commands.description: Gets the Layout Info Panel custom field definitions (name and key) from Book Settings.

commands.name: GetModelViewOptions
commands.description: Gets all model view options

commands.name: GetViewSettings
commands.description: Gets the view settings of navigator items

commands.name: SetViewSettings
commands.description: Sets the view settings of navigator items

commands.name: GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination
commands.description: Gets the graphic override combination applied to the current window, with its id and name. The response is empty when no combination is applied. This is the combination of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 30.

commands.name: SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination
commands.description: Applies a graphic override combination, given by id or by name, to the current window. The current window must be a model window (floor plan, section, elevation, 3D, ...). To remove the overrides, apply the project's 'No Overrides' combination. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 30.

inputScheme.description: The graphic override combination to apply, given by id or by name.

combinationId.description: The identifier of the graphic override combination, as returned by GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination.

name.description: The name of the graphic override combination, as shown in Document > Graphic Overrides > Graphic Override Combinations.

commands.name: GetView2DTransformations
commands.description: Get zoom and rotation of 2D views

commands.name: SetViewRotation
commands.description: Set the rotation angle of 2D views via their floor plan database.

commands.name: CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap
commands.description: Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.

viewsData.description: Array of views to clone from the Project Map to the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the Project Map viewpoint to clone.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the View Map folder to place the clone in. Required - Archicad's CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap API leaves a clone created directly at the View Map root in a broken state (it cannot be deleted or moved afterwards, by API or by hand), so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

commands.name: CreateViewsInViewMap
commands.description: Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items.

viewsData.description: Array of views to create as independent (non-clone) items in the View Map.

navigatorItemId.description: Source navigator item whose database and settings are copied.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: View Map folder to place the new view in. Required - the underlying Archicad API used to create the item leaves it undeletable and unmovable afterwards when it is attached directly to the View Map root, so Tapir refuses to fall back to the root on your behalf. Create a View Map folder (CreateViewMapFolder) first if you don't already have one to target.

name.description: Name for the new view. Optional; defaults to the source item name.

commands.name: CreateViewMapFolder
commands.description: Creates a new folder in the View Map.

folderName.description: Name of the new folder to create in the View Map.

parentNavigatorItemId.description: Navigator item ID of the parent View Map folder. Optional; defaults to the View Map root.

commands.name: Set3DCutPlanes
commands.description: Sets the 3D cut planes.

items.description: Defines a 3D cut plane using the plane equation: pa*x + pb*y + pc*z + pd = 0

pa.description: Coefficient of x in the plane equation. The x coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pb.description: Coefficient of y in the plane equation. The y coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pc.description: Coefficient of z in the plane equation. The z coordinate of the normal vector of the plane.

pd.description: Constant term in the plane equation. The distance of the plane from the origin along the normal vector.

commands.name: Get3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the transformation matrix of an axonometry.

commands.name: Set3DProjectionSettings
commands.description: Sets a perspective projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced.

commands.name: FitInWindow
commands.description: Zooms to the given elements or fits everything in the window.

commands.name: CreateSections
commands.description: Creates Section elements on the floor plan.

commands.name: CreateInteriorElevations
commands.description: Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room.

interiorElevationsData.description: Array of data to create Interior Elevation elements.

commands.name: MoveNavigatorItem
commands.description: Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree.

commands.name: RenameNavigatorItem
commands.description: Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. Fails when Archicad does not apply the new name (e.g. on Project Map schedule items, which are named by their scheme). With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

customName.description: Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.

commands.name: DeleteNavigatorItems
commands.description: Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree.

commands.name: GetNavigatorItemTree
commands.description: Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map.

publisherSetName.description: The name of the publisher set to retrieve. Used only when navigatorMapId is PublisherSets. Without it the first publisher set is returned.

commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideRule
commands.description: Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

name.description: Name of the override rule. Rule names are unique in the project: an existing rule with this name is overwritten, in whichever rule group it is.

ruleGroupName.description: Rule group of a new rule, created when it does not exist. Default: 'Tapir'. An overwritten rule stays in its own group.

criterionXML.description: Optional criterion XML. Archicad only takes XML in its own format: read it from a rule made in the GUI with GetGraphicalOverrideRules and change the values. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and so is an empty one: the rule then applies to all elements.

surfaceRGB.description: Optional color override of the cut and uncut surfaces. Components are in the 0..1 range.

linePenIndex.description: Optional pen index override for lines, markers and texts. Only a positive index takes effect.

overrideContours.description: Optional. If true, the contours of the overridden surfaces are recolored too.

commands.name: GetGraphicalOverrideRules
commands.description: Returns every graphic override rule with its criterion XML. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination
commands.description: Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

name.description: Name of the override combination. When a combination with this name exists, its rule list is replaced.

ruleNames.description: Names of the override rules in the combination, in order. Rule names are unique in the project, whatever the rule group. An empty list makes a combination without rules.

commands.name: CreateIssue
commands.description: Creates a new issue.

name.description: The name of the issue.

tagText.description: Tag text of the issue, optional.

commands.name: DeleteIssue
commands.description: Deletes the specified issue.

acceptAllElements.description: Accept all creation/deletion/modification of the deleted issue. By default false.

commands.name: GetIssues
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing issues.

commands.name: AddCommentToIssue
commands.description: Adds a new comment to the specified issue.

author.description: The author of the new comment.

commands.name: GetCommentsFromIssue
commands.description: Retrieves comments information from the specified issue.

commands.name: AttachElementsToIssue
commands.description: Attaches elements to the specified issue.

commands.name: DetachElementsFromIssue
commands.description: Detaches elements from the specified issue.

commands.name: GetElementsAttachedToIssue
commands.description: Retrieves attached elements of the specified issue, filtered by attachment type.

commands.name: ExportIssuesToBCF
commands.description: Exports specified issues to a BCF file.

issues.description: Leave it empty to export all issues.

exportPath.description: The os path to the bcf file, including it's name.

useExternalId.description: Use external IFC ID or Archicad IFC ID as referenced in BCF topics.

alignBySurveyPoint.description: Align BCF views by Archicad Survey Point or Archicad Project Origin.

commands.name: ImportIssuesFromBCF
commands.description: Imports issues from the specified BCF file.

importPath.description: The os path to the bcf file, including it's name.

alignBySurveyPoint.description: Align BCF views by Archicad Survey Point or Archicad Project Origin.

commands.name: GetRevisionIssues
commands.description: Retrieves all issues.

commands.name: GetRevisionChanges
commands.description: Retrieves all changes.

commands.name: GetDocumentRevisions
commands.description: Retrieves all document revisions.

commands.name: GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts
commands.description: Retrieves all changes belong to the last revision of the given layouts.

commands.name: GetRevisionChangesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the changes belong to the given elements.

commands.name: GetDesignOptions
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design options. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: GetDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: GetDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design option combinations.

commands.name: GetElementsOfDesignOptions
commands.description: Retrieves the elements associated with the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: GetDesignOptionForElements
commands.description: Retrieves the design option association for the specified elements. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Creates new design option sets with the given names. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateDesignOptions
commands.description: Creates new design options with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Creates new design option combinations with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations
commands.description: Sets active design options in the given combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

activeDesignOptions.description: The list of active design options in the combination.

commands.name: MoveElementsToDesignOptions
commands.description: Moves the given elements into the given design options. Use NULLGuid for design option to remove the element from any design options and move it to the main model. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionId.description: The identifier of the design option to move the element into. Use NULLGuid to remove the element from any design option and move it to the main model.

commands.name: MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet
commands.description: Moves the given design options to another sets. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionId.description: The identifier of the design option to move.

commands.name: RenameDesignOptions
commands.description: Changes the name and/or the string id of the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

name.description: The new name of the design option. The name is kept when it is not given.

id.description: The new string id of the design option. The id is kept when it is not given.

designOptions.description: The design options to rename, each with the new name and/or id. At least one of them must be given.

commands.name: RenameDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Changes the name of the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

name.description: The new name of the design option set.

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to rename, each with the new name.

commands.name: RenameDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Changes the name of the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

name.description: The new name of the design option combination.

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to rename, each with the new name.

commands.name: DeleteDesignOptions
commands.description: Deletes the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: DeleteDesignOptionSets
commands.description: Deletes the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionSets.description: The design option sets to delete.

commands.name: DeleteDesignOptionCombinations
commands.description: Deletes the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

designOptionCombinations.description: The design option combinations to delete.

commands.name: GetKeynoteTree
commands.description: Retrieves the whole keynote folder and item hierarchy. The technical root folder is not included in the output; the top-level folders and items are returned directly. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: GetKeynoteAutoTexts
commands.description: Retrieves the autotext tokens of the given keynote items. The tokens can be used as label text content to reference the fields of a keynote item. Available from Archicad 28.

keynoteItems.description: The keynote items to get the autotext tokens for.

commands.name: CreateKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Creates keynote folders under the given parent folders (or under the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.

foldersData.description: Array of data to create keynote folders.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

commands.name: CreateKeynoteItems
commands.description: Creates keynote items in the given parent folders (or in the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.

itemsData.description: Array of data to create keynote items.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

commands.name: ModifyKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Modifies the key, title or reference of the given keynote folders. Available from Archicad 28.

foldersData.description: Array of data to modify keynote folders. Only provided fields are changed.

commands.name: ModifyKeynoteItems
commands.description: Modifies the key, title, description or reference of the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.

itemsData.description: Array of data to modify keynote items. Only provided fields are changed.

commands.name: DeleteKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Deletes the given keynote folders including their content. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: DeleteKeynoteItems
commands.description: Deletes the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: CreateKeynoteLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create keynote labels.

position.description: The reference point of the label.

contentFields.description: The keynote fields to include in the label text as autotext. Optional; defaults to all fields.

commands.name: GetMEPElements
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project, optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

elementTypes.description: Optional filter for the MEP element types.

domains.description: Optional filter for the MEP domains.

commands.name: GetMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id) and nodes. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: GetMEPPorts
commands.description: Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size and connection status. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: GetMEPDistributionSystems
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute and member elements. Available from Archicad 28.

commands.name: CreateMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions). Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP routing elements.

nodeCoordinates.description: The corner points of the route polyline.

crossSectionWidth.description: Optional cross section width applied to all segments.

crossSectionHeight.description: Optional cross section height applied to all segments.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: Optional cross section reference id of the segment preference table (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table of the current routing tool default.

preferenceTableId.description: Optional guid of the segment preference table (see GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index of the routing element and all its parts (routing segments, rigid segments, elbows and transitions). Only a positive index takes effect; otherwise the routing tool default layer is used. A layer that does not exist or is locked gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

commands.name: CreateMEPElements
commands.description: Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions. Available from Archicad 28.

elementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP elements.

domain.description: Required for all types except Equipment.

orientationDirection.description: Optional direction vector of the orientation. Defaults to (1, 0, 0).

orientationRotation.description: Optional rotation vector of the orientation. Defaults to (0, 1, 0).

commands.name: ModifyMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id) of all segments and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP routing elements. Only provided fields are changed.

crossSectionWidth.description: New cross section width applied to all segments.

crossSectionHeight.description: New cross section height applied to all segments.

crossSectionShape.description: The new shape is applied to all segments.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: New cross section reference id of the segment preference table applied to all segments (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table the segments already use.

preferenceTableId.description: New segment preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.

nodePositions.description: New positions of the routing nodes. The size must match the number of nodes of the route.

commands.name: ConnectMEPElements
commands.description: Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. Available from Archicad 28.

connectToId.description: The MEP element or routing element to connect to.

commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTables
commands.description: Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Available from Archicad 28.

includeFittingTables.description: Also return the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. Defaults to false.

commands.name: GetMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.

commands.name: CreateMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to create system groups.

commands.name: CreateMEPPhysicalSystems
commands.description: Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29.

physicalSystemsData.description: Array of data to create physical systems.

systemGroupId.description: The system group the new physical system belongs to.

rootElementId.description: The MEP element the system starts from. Archicad keeps it only while it is part of an MEP network: the root of a stand-alone element is cleared when the MEP networks are recalculated.

mepSystemId.description: The MEP system attribute used as the category of the physical system.

commands.name: GetElectricalPanels
commands.description: Gets the electrical panels (distribution boards) of the project or the given ones: name, circuit naming, circuits, parent circuit, placement and the connected and demand loads in total and per phase. Available from Archicad 30.

elements.description: Optional list of electrical panels. Every electrical panel of the project is returned when it is not given.

commands.name: GetElectricalCircuits
commands.description: Gets the given electrical circuits, the circuits of the given panels, or every circuit of the project: name, description, owner panel, connected devices and panels, voltage, phases, wiring type, loads, voltage drop and estimated cable length. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalPanels.description: Optional list of electrical panels whose circuits are returned. When neither elements nor electricalPanels is given, every circuit of every electrical panel of the project is returned.

commands.name: GetElectricalDevices
commands.description: Gets the electrical devices (lights, sockets and other consumers) of the project or the given ones: parent circuit, placement, apparent power, load classification, demand load and directly connected MEP elements. Available from Archicad 30.

elements.description: Optional list of electrical devices. Every electrical device of the project is returned when it is not given.

commands.name: GetElectricalProjectSettings
commands.description: Gets the electrical project settings: the default voltage, the wiring types with their cross-sectional area and the load classifications with their demand factor. Available from Archicad 30.

commands.name: CreateElectricalPanels
commands.description: Places electrical panels with the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, panel name and circuit naming. Available from Archicad 30.

electricalPanelsData.description: Array of data to create electrical panels. The fields that are not given are taken from the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool.

position.description: The anchor point of the new panel.

orientation.description: Defaults to the direction (1, 0, 0) and the rotation (0, 1, 0).

libraryPartId.description: The library part to use, as listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

xSize.description: The size along the local x axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

ySize.description: The size along the local y axis. Some library parts calculate their own size, then the item fails.

commands.name: CreateElectricalDevices

MorphBody.description: A Morph's full body geometry: an indexed vertex list plus one entry per face (polygon). Shared shape between GetDetailsOfElements' output and CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs' input - what Get reports is what Create/Modify accept back. There is no fillet/chamfer operation in the Archicad API - a caller wanting rounded geometry must supply the already-tessellated facets here; edgeOverrides only controls how an existing straight edge is DISPLAYED (hidden/visible/smooth-shaded), not its shape.

bodyType.description: Whether the body is a closed solid or an open surface shell. Reported accurately on Get; on Create/Modify this is set on the element but a confirmed Archicad SDK bug means it may not take effect (bodyType has been observed always coming back Solid regardless of what was requested - see edgeOverrides' note).

isClosed.description: READ-ONLY, Get output only (ignored if sent to Create/Modify). Geometrically computed (Modeler::MeshBody::IsClosedBody): true if every edge in the body has exactly two adjacent faces (a watertight/manifold volume), false if any edge borders only one face (an open shell / has holes or gaps). Distinct from bodyType, which is the caller's declared INTENT (Solid vs Surface) rather than the actual computed geometry - a body can be declared bodyType 'Solid' yet still be geometrically open if a face is missing.

edgeDefault.description: Default display status for every edge that has no entry in edgeOverrides. Reported accurately on Get. On Create/Modify it takes effect from Archicad 29 on, where it is applied to every edge of the element with ACAPI_Element_ChangeMorphEdgeType right after the element is created or changed (e.g. 'HardHidden' hides all edges of a triangulated body). On Archicad 28 and earlier it is set on the element but does not take effect due to the same confirmed Archicad SDK bug as edgeOverrides (element.morph.edgeType is silently discarded by ACAPI_Element_Create/Change).

vertices.description: Flat, indexed vertex list, local to the Morph's own placement (not world coordinates). A Solid body needs at least 4 (a tetrahedron, the minimum closed volume); a Surface body has no closedness requirement at all - the minimum is 2 vertices joined by a single wireEdge (a lone vertex with no edge at all is rejected by Archicad itself, confirmed live) - enforced with a bodyType-aware error message, not by this minItems floor alone.

polygons.description: One entry per face loop (into `vertices`), counterclockwise as seen from outside the body. Optional - a body made entirely of wireEdges (see below) needs none. Set "filled": false on an entry to create only that loop's edges (e.g. the outline of a pyramid's side faces) without an actual filled face.

wireEdges.description: Standalone edges that belong to no face at all (e.g. a bare rectangle outline, or a pyramid with a filled base but wireframe-only sides - set "filled": false on a polygons entry for a whole closed loop like that instead, this is for individual edges not already covered by any polygon loop). Reported accurately by GetDetailsOfElements (every edge with zero adjacent faces); accepted back by CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs. Identifies an edge by the (unordered) pair of vertex indices it connects - reuses whatever edge already exists between those two vertices if the polygons above happen to share it.

edgeOverrides.description: READ-ONLY in practice: reported accurately by GetDetailsOfElements (reflecting whatever Archicad itself currently has), but CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs silently ignore this field on input - per-edge display status cannot be set by an add-on due to a confirmed, still-unresolved Archicad SDK bug (element.morph.edgeType/bodyType are silently discarded by ACAPI_Element_Create/Change; see the GRAPHISOFT community forum thread 'Help with setting morph's hidden edges in the API'). To hide or smooth ALL edges of a Morph use edgeDefault, which does take effect from Archicad 29 on. Sparse when present - only edges whose display status differs from edgeDefault get an entry. Identifies an edge by the (unordered) pair of vertex indices it connects.

smooth.description: Shade the two adjacent faces smoothly across this edge instead of as a hard crease - the 'aide a la courbe' rounded-look hint. Does not change actual geometry.

silhouetteOnly.description: Show this edge's line only where it forms a silhouette/contour from the current viewpoint.

origin.description: Translation component of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's origin column).

xAxis.description: X axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's first column). Omit on Create to get an identity rotation; give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.

yAxis.description: Y axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's second column). Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.

zAxis.description: Z axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's third column). Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.

buildingMaterialId.description: The Morph's building material - a single, whole-volume property (what the mass is 'made of', governing cut-fill/quantity takeoff), NOT settable per face. Per-face appearance is controlled separately by each polygon's own surfaceId (see MorphBody) - confirmed live these are two independent, unrelated attributes (a Morph can have one uniform building material while showing a different Surface finish on each face).

surfaceId.description: The Morph's own default Surface (element.morph.material) - used for any face that has no per-face surfaceId override of its own (see MorphBody polygons[].surfaceId). Distinct from buildingMaterialId (the whole-volume material). Confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this specific field when set through ACAPI_Element_Create alone (reproduced identically on Archicad 27 and 29 - not a version-specific issue, unlike polygons[].surfaceId below); CreateMorphs works around this transparently with an internal follow-up Change right after Create, so this field behaves correctly end-to-end despite the underlying quirk.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true, the per-story visibility (showContour/showFill) is calculated automatically from the Morph's vertical extent instead of using the explicit values.

GraphicOverrideCriterion.description: Structured conditions of a graphic override rule, turned into Archicad's criterion XML (an alternative to criterionXML). Give exactly one property. 'and'/'or' combine a flat list of other conditions (no nesting, see their description). 'elementType' filters by the tool an element was created with; 'all3DTypes'/'all2DTypes' match every 3D or 2D element. The other properties are conditions of Archicad's criteria editor: classification, layer and Model View, Construction, Positioning, Plan and Section, Surfaces and Materials, ID and Categories, Geometry, custom properties, and fields of the Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Object/Lamp, Door/Window, Opening, Curtain Wall and Stair tools. Their identifiers were captured from rules made in the criteria editor of Archicad 29; Archicad 27 keeps the generated rules as well. Not available: the renovation status of an element, and the shape, limits and orientation of an Opening.

name.description: The profile modifier parameter's name, exactly as defined on the Complex Profile attribute.

customPropertyBool.description: Matches elements by a custom (user-defined) boolean property, identified by its plain name and the name of the property group it appears under (both exactly as shown in the Property Manager). Provide 'name', 'group', and exactly one of the operators below. The 6 'has.../is...' operators are available on every custom property type, not just boolean ones.

name.description: The custom property's name, exactly as defined.

group.description: The custom property group's name, exactly as defined (e.g. 'Generalites').

equals.description: Matches if the property's value equals this.

hasDefaultValue.description: If true, matches elements where this property currently has its default value.

hasCustomValue.description: If true, matches elements where this property has a custom (overridden, non-default) value.

isAvailable.description: If true, matches elements where this property is available.

isNotAvailable.description: If true, matches elements where this property is not available.

isUndefined.description: If true, matches elements where this property is undefined.

isNotUndefined.description: If true, matches elements where this property is not undefined.

group.description: The custom property group's name, exactly as defined.

equals.description: Matches if the property's value equals this string exactly.

notEquals.description: Matches if the property's value does not equal this string.

surfaceColor.description: The color that replaces the surface of elements. Use either this or surface.

overridePenColorAndThickness.description: Override the pen color and thickness.
